note: Root (2026-11-21): Filed under נקב 'pierce, bore': the verb is scripture's own (2Ki 12:10 וַיִּקֹּב חֹר, Hag 1:6), Arabic نَقَبَ 'perforated, bored' (Lane p. 2833), and נְקֵבָה is its feminine qᵉṭēlā form; how 'female' comes from piercing is not shown by the verses. Other words of the root (נֶקֶב, מַקֶּבֶת if so filed) would join this entry.
summary: נְקֵבָה designates a female. Genesis pairs it with זָכָר, ‘male,’ both for humankind at creation and for the animals entering the ark.

evidence.note: The closing clause describes the humans God created as זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה, “male and female.”
Two of each are to enter the ark. זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה specifies one male and one female.

opposites.note: The verse pairs the terms for male and female.
